title: Check: Services
description: Five questions on the four Service types and how they route.

questions.prompt: What does a ClusterIP Service give you?

options.text: An address reachable from outside the cluster
A stable virtual IP reachable only from inside the cluster
A DNS name only, with no IP

questions.explanation: ClusterIP is the default and the building block: NodePort and LoadBalancer are layered on top of one.

questions.prompt: What is the default NodePort range?
questions.explanation: Configurable with --service-node-port-range on the API server, but 30000-32767 is what you should expect.

questions.prompt: A Service selects Pods but sends traffic nowhere. What do you check first?

options.text: Its EndpointSlices - whether any ready Pod matches the selector

questions.explanation: `kubectl get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=<svc>`. Empty means the selector matches nothing ready.

questions.prompt: Write the command that exposes a Deployment named web on port 80 as a ClusterIP Service.
questions.explanation: Add `--target-port` when the container listens on a different port.

options.text: A headless Service: DNS returns Pod IPs directly, with no VIP

questions.explanation: Headless Services are how StatefulSets give each Pod its own resolvable name.
